title: Arvehyldingseden for Island - the hereditary homage oath for Iceland sworn at Kopavogur
exact_locator: Lovsamling for Island I (1096-1720), Copenhagen 1853, p. 273: 'Arvehyldingseden for Island. Kopavog 28. Juli 1662'; the edition's own provenance note reads 'Afskrift i det kongelige Bibliotheks Nye kongel. Saml. Nr. 1265, Fol.'
statement: The oath binds the swearer to Frederick III as hereditary and absolute king; it opens 'Eg N. N. lofa og tilsegi, ad vera theim stormektugasta fursta og herra, kong Fridrich theim thridja, Danmerkur, Noregs...' - the Danish-Norwegian royal style, sworn for Iceland.
interpretation: This is the constitutional title by which Iceland is under the Danish-Norwegian crown at the snapshot, and it is Iceland's own act, sworn on Icelandic soil. The Faroes swore separately at Thorshavn on 14 August 1662 - which is exactly why the Faroes are not inherited from this assertion.

title: Resolution of the syslumenn at the Althing, 16 July 1756, on poor relief and the suppression of vagrancy
exact_locator: TI. Skjalasafn amtmanns. II. 42A. Bref ur Mulasyslu 1724-1756. Bref ur Mulathingi 1724-1756 (Bref til konungs d. 20. jan. 1755 og alyktun syslumanna d. 16. juli 1756)
statement: The king's district magistrates, assembled at the Althing, resolved on how to improve poor relief and curb begging and vagrancy in the districts; the resolution is filed in the archive of the amtmadur over all Iceland.
interpretation: An individually dated act of Iceland's own royal administration, sixteen days BEFORE the snapshot, held in the fonds of the crown's chief officer for the island. It shows the administration governing, not merely existing.

title: Letter of amtmadur Magnus Gislason to the government offices in Copenhagen on the effect of the Katla eruption on the king's estates, 4 August 1756
exact_locator: TI. Skjalasafn amtmanns. I. 11. Brefabok 1756-1757, bls. 63-65 (Bref d. 4. agust 1756)
statement: The amtmadur reports to the central government on the damage done by the 1755 Katla eruption to his majesty's farms in Iceland.
interpretation: Three days after the snapshot, and kept for two reasons: it is direct evidence of crown landholding being administered on the island, and it is the contemporary record behind the volcanic entry in the coastal-change audit. The letter-book runs continuously from 1 July 1756, so the office was writing across the snapshot instant itself.

title: Distribution of the gjafakorn - the king's gift grain - to distressed farmers, December 1756
exact_locator: TI. Skjalasafn amtmanns. I. 11. Brefabok 1756-1757, bls. 254-264 (Bref d. 5.-27. des. 1756); see also the box 'Skjol um gjafakornid 1756-1758'
statement: At the end of 1756 meal sent by the crown was distributed to destitute farmers in the districts around the seat of the amtmadur, and the operation generated its own file.
interpretation: A crown relief operation executed through the island administration in the snapshot year.
